name: Business Continuity - Automatic Incident Coordination During Outages

parameters.content:
## Business Continuity: Automatic Team Coordination During Outages

### How it works

Turns a monitoring alert into a coordinated response without anyone having to organize it by hand.

1. **Declare:** an alert (`POST /bc-alert`, simple JSON or Prometheus Alertmanager) opens one incident per service. Further alerts for the same service attach to it, so there are no duplicate war rooms.
2. **Coordinate:** a Slack war room is created and gets the brief, first-response checklist and runbook. Who is paged depends on severity: the service owner always, dependent teams and customer communications from SEV2, executives on SEV1. Each person gets an email with their own acknowledge link.
3. **Acknowledge:** the first responder to click becomes incident commander and escalation stops.
4. **Escalate:** with no acknowledgement (SEV1 5 min, SEV2 15, SEV3 60) it moves up: team lead, engineering director, CTO.
5. **Keep everyone informed:** SEV1 gets a stakeholder update every 30 minutes, SEV2 every 60, built from the incident timeline.
6. **Resolve:** the commander calls `POST /bc-resolve` with a summary. Duration is posted, stakeholders are emailed and a post-incident review due date is set.

Everything is written to an incident timeline table for the review.

### Setup steps

- Add Postgres, SMTP (email) and Slack credentials (Header Auth `Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...` with `channels:manage` and `chat:write` scopes), then run the manual setup once.
- Edit **Set Continuity Config**: your n8n webhook base URL, sender email, default Slack channel id, executive, comms and stakeholder emails, ack and update timings.
- Replace the demo teams and services with your own.
- Point your monitoring at `POST /bc-alert` with `{"service":"payments-api","title":"High error rate","severity":"critical","description":"..."}` and activate the workflow.

### Layout

1 Setup
2-4 Entry, intake and declaration
5-6 Acknowledge and resolve
7-9 Monitor, escalate and status updates

## 1. One-time setup

Run manually once. Creates teams, services (tier, owner, dependent teams, runbook steps), incidents with a one-open-incident-per-service rule, and a timeline table, plus demo data.

## 2. Entry points & routing

Monitoring alerts, responder acknowledgements, resolutions and a 5-minute monitor all share one configuration and are routed to their own pipeline.

## 3. Alert intake & dedupe

`POST /bc-alert` accepts a simple payload or Prometheus Alertmanager. One incident is opened per service, repeat alerts are attached to it, and recovery signals are posted to the war room.

## 4. Declare incident & coordinate teams

For a new incident: load the service and team contacts, decide who to pull in by severity, create a Slack war room, post the brief and runbook checklist, and email every responder an acknowledge link.

## 5. Acknowledge incident

`GET /bc-ack` from the email or Slack link, checked with a secret token. The first responder becomes incident commander and escalation stops.

## 6. Resolve incident

`POST /bc-resolve` with the commander's token and a summary. Closes the incident, posts the duration to the war room, emails stakeholders and sets the post-incident review due date.

nodes.name: Note: 7. Monitor: find incidents needing action

parameters.content:
## 7. Monitor: find incidents needing action

Every 5 minutes: finds unacknowledged incidents past their limit (SEV1 5 min, SEV2 15, SEV3 60) and incidents due a status update.

## 8. Escalate unacknowledged incidents

Moves up the chain (team lead, engineering director, CTO), emails the next person with an acknowledge link and warns the war room.

## 9. Periodic status updates

SEV1 every 30 minutes and SEV2 every 60 minutes: posts the latest timeline entry to the war room and emails stakeholders.

parameters.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bc_teams (
  team        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  oncall_email TEXT NOT NULL,
  lead_email   TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bc_services (
  service_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name            TEXT NOT NULL,
  tier            INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 3,
  owner_team      TEXT REFERENCES bc_teams (team),
  dependent_teams JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  customer_facing BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  runbook_url     TEXT,
  runbook_steps   JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bc_incidents (
  incident_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  service_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
  title              TEXT NOT NULL,
  severity           TEXT NOT NULL,
  status             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  alert_count        INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  first_alert        JSONB,
  ack_token          TEXT NOT NULL,
  resolve_token      TEXT NOT NULL,
  slack_channel_id   TEXT,
  escalation_level   INT  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  declared_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  acknowledged_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
  acknowledged_by    TEXT,
  last_escalated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ,
  last_update_at     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  resolved_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
  resolution_summary TEXT,
  root_cause         TEXT,
  updated_at         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
-- One open incident per service: further alerts for it are attached instead of opening a duplicate
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS uq_bc_open_per_service ON bc_incidents (service_id) WHERE status <> 'resolved';
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bc_incident_events (
  id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  incident_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  event       TEXT NOT NULL,
  actor       TEXT,
  detail      TEXT,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Demo data: replace with your own teams and services
INSERT INTO bc_teams (team, oncall_email, lead_email) VALUES
  ('payments', 'user@example.com', 'user@example.com'),
  ('platform', 'user@example.com', 'user@example.com'),
  ('support',  'user@example.com',  'user@example.com'),
  ('it',       'user@example.com',       'user@example.com')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
INSERT INTO bc_services (service_id, name, tier, owner_team, dependent_teams, customer_facing, runbook_url, runbook_steps) VALUES
  ('payments-api', 'Payments API', 1, 'payments', '["platform","support"]', TRUE, 'https://wiki.example.com/runbooks/payments-api',
   '["Check the payment provider status page","Check recent deploys and roll back if one is correlated","Verify database and queue health","Enable the fallback payment route if available"]'),
  ('internal-wiki', 'Internal Wiki', 3, 'it', '[]', FALSE, NULL, '["Restart the wiki service","Check disk space"]')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
SELECT 'continuity_ready' AS status;

WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO bc_incidents (incident_id, service_id, title, severity, first_alert, ack_token, resolve_token, last_update_at)
  VALUES ($1::text, $2::text, $3::text, $4::text, $5::jsonb, $6::text, $7::text, NOW())
  ON CONFLICT (service_id) WHERE status <> 'resolved' DO NOTHING
  RETURNING incident_id, severity
), att AS (
  UPDATE bc_incidents SET alert_count = alert_count + 1, severity = LEAST(severity, $4::text), updated_at = NOW()
  WHERE service_id = $2::text AND status <> 'resolved' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ins)
  RETURNING incident_id, severity
), ev AS (
  INSERT INTO bc_incident_events (incident_id, event, actor, detail)
  SELECT incident_id, 'declared', 'monitoring', $3::text FROM ins
  UNION ALL SELECT incident_id, 'alert_attached', 'monitoring', $3::text FROM att
  RETURNING 1
)
SELECT incident_id, severity, TRUE AS is_new FROM ins
UNION ALL SELECT incident_id, severity, FALSE AS is_new FROM att;

SELECT s.service_id, s.name, s.tier, s.owner_team, s.customer_facing, s.runbook_url, s.runbook_steps, ot.oncall_email, ot.lead_email,
       COALESCE((SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('team', t.team, 'email', t.oncall_email)) FROM bc_teams t
                 WHERE t.team IN (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text(s.dependent_teams))), '[]'::jsonb) AS dependents
FROM (SELECT $1::text AS service_id) q
LEFT JOIN bc_services s ON s.service_id = q.service_id
LEFT JOIN bc_teams ot ON ot.team = s.owner_team;

SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT i.incident_id, i.title, i.severity, i.status, i.slack_channel_id, i.escalation_level, i.declared_at, i.acknowledged_by, i.alert_count, i.ack_token,
         t.lead_email AS owner_lead,
         ROUND((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (NOW() - i.declared_at)) / 60)::numeric)::int AS open_min,
         (SELECT e.detail FROM bc_incident_events e WHERE e.incident_id = i.incident_id ORDER BY e.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS last_event,
         CASE
           WHEN i.status = 'open'
            AND NOW() - COALESCE(i.last_escalated_at, i.declared_at) > (CASE i.severity WHEN 'SEV1' THEN $1::int WHEN 'SEV2' THEN $2::int ELSE $3::int END) * INTERVAL '1 minute'
           THEN 'escalate'
           WHEN (CASE i.severity WHEN 'SEV1' THEN $4::int WHEN 'SEV2' THEN $5::int ELSE 0 END) > 0
            AND NOW() - i.last_update_at > (CASE i.severity WHEN 'SEV1' THEN $4::int ELSE $5::int END) * INTERVAL '1 minute'
           THEN 'status_update'
         END AS action
  FROM bc_incidents i
  LEFT JOIN bc_services s ON s.service_id = i.service_id
  LEFT JOIN bc_teams t ON t.team = s.owner_team
  WHERE i.status <> 'resolved'
) x WHERE action IS NOT NULL ORDER BY declared_at;
